questions.problem:
Which of the following subspaces must be orthogonal to $\text{Col}(A)$ for every matrix $A?$

- $\text{Col}({A}^{T})$
- $\text{Null}({A}^{T})$
- $\text{Null}(A)$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that $\text{Col}(A)$ consists of all linear combinations of the columns of $A$, that is, the rows of ${A}^{T}.$

If a vector is orthogonal to every linear combination of the rows of ${A}^{T},$ it must be orthogonal to each row of ${A}^{T}.$
But notice that when pre-multiplying a vector by ${A}^{T},$ we actually multiply each row of ${A}^{T}$ by that vector.
So, $\text{Col}(A)$ must be orthogonal to the left null space of $A,$ which is $\text{Null}({A}^{T}).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

**Note:** In general, the four fundamental subspaces of a matrix $A$ can be schematically visualized, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14114441/assets/de22dd5b352e1d5be48f4b6ed3b2a4657ae623c1bd288d3464559758ea334af7.png)

questions.problem: Let $A$ be a $m\times n$ matrix. What is the image of ${R}^{m}$ under the action of ${A}^{T}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that ${A}^{T}$ is a $n\times m$ matrix.

Pre-multiplying a vector $x\in {R}^{m}$ by ${A}^{T}$ gives a linear combination of the columns of ${A}^{T}:$

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}| & | & ⋯ & | \\ {a}_{1}^{T} & {a}_{2}^{T} & ⋯ & {a}_{m}^{T} \\ | & | & ⋯ & |\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{A}^{T}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{m}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}={x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}| \\ {a}_{1}^{T} \\ |\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}| \\ {a}_{2}^{T} \\ |\end{aligned}]+⋯+{x}_{m}[\begin{aligned}| \\ {a}_{m}^{T} \\ |\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the image of ${R}^{m}$ under the action of ${A}^{T}$ must be $\text{Col}({A}^{T}),$ the row space of $A.$

questions.problem: Let $A$ and $B$ be $m\times p$ and $p\times n$ matrices, respectively. What is the image of $\text{Col}({B}^{T}\,{A}^{T})$ under the action of $AB?$
questions.worked_solution:
Pre-multiplying a vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ by $AB$ gives a linear combination of the columns of $AB:$

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}| & | & ⋯ & | \\ (ab)_{1} & (ab)_{2} & ⋯ & (ab)_{n} \\ | & | & ⋯ & |\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{AB}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}={x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}| \\ (ab)_{1} \\ |\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}| \\ (ab)_{2} \\ |\end{aligned}]+⋯+{x}_{n}[\begin{aligned}| \\ (ab)_{n} \\ |\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the image of ${R}^{n}$ under the action of $AB$ must be $\text{Col}(AB),$ the column space of $AB.$

Furthermore, since $\text{Null}(AB)$ is mapped to the zero vector $0$ by the definition of the null subspace, the image of its orthogonal complement $\text{Col}((AB)^{T})=\text{Col}({B}^{T}\,{A}^{T})$ must be $\text{Col}(AB).$

This can be schematically visualized, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14114441/assets/885bf8a3061f93ad400897a7273ffe4157d22dee20b8e4ee7ebb982b1c4319bb.png)
